Re: LD 990, Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an Optional Online Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations

Dear Senator Carney and Representative Kuhn:

I am writing in opposition to L.D. 990, Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an Optional Online Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations. The bill requires the Attorney General to develop an "optional online landlord registry for landlords renting rooms within their primary residences." The registry must provide information to landlords regarding their "rights and obligations as landlords."

As I understand it, the bill is intended assist persons who rent rooms in their homes in understanding their rights and obligations as landlords. It is not clear why a registry would be necessary, though. The goal could be accomplished by simply having a brochure or website providing information for landlords. It is also not clear why this bill is limited to landlords who are renting rooms within their primary residence and does not include, for example, landlords who rent apartment units within their residences or in separate premises.

In any event, with respect to housing, the focus of my office's Consumer Protection Division is on tenants, and our Consumer Law Guide addresses tenant rights.1 This information may be helpful for landlords inasmuch as it addresses some of their legal obligations. It would not be appropriate, though, for my office to go beyond what is in the Guide and provide advice to landlords about their rights vis-�-vis tenants.

I trust this information is helpful.

1 See https://www.maine.gov/ag/consumer/consumer_law_guide.shtml.

Senator Anne Carney, Senate Chair Representative Amy Kuhn, House Chair March 24, 2025 Page 2
Sincerely,
Aaron M. Frey Attorney General

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary March 24, 2025
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee
on Judiciary, my name is Chip Curry. I represent Senate District ll, which is all of the 26 rural, coastal, and island communities of Waldo County. Thank you for the opportunity to present LD 990, a
"Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an Optional Online
Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations."
The increasingly tight housing market in Maine has led to a rise in homeowners renting out spare rooms to offset living expenses and stay in their homes. This trend is particularly prevalent among older Mainers. However, many homeowners have limited experience acting as landlords and often do not know where to turn for reliable guidance on rental agreements, tenant screening, or eviction procedures. As a result, small-scale landlords can quickly become vulnerable to nonpayment of rent or
other legal complications, and tenants can find themselves in confusing or unsafe situations if their landlords do not know their legal obligations.
This concern was brought to my attention by a constituent who encountered serious challenges
collecting rent and navigating the months-long eviction process while renting a room in their primary residence. Unfortunately, this scenario is not unique, and with new initiatives like Maine's Homeshare Pilot Program, more Mainers are opening their homes to tenants and facing the potential pitfalls of
landlord-tenant relationships without sufficient resources to protect themselves or their tenants.
LD 990 would address these challenges by directing the Office of the Attorney General to develop and
promote an optional online registry specifically tailored for homeowners renting out rooms. Landlords who opt into this registry would have access to clear, user-friendly materials outlining landlord responsibilities, tenant rights, and legally sound eviction procedures. This registry would be regularly updated by the Office of the Attorney General to reflect any future legislative changes, ensuring that guidance remains accurate and relevant.
The bill aims to protect property owners and tenants from the outset by proactively educating
homeowners. Landlords who understand their duties under Maine law --- from drafting thorough rental
agreements to the requirements of fair eviction procedures -- are more informed when setting rental
rates and less likely to encounter costly, time-consuming legal conflicts. In turn, tenants benefit from
having a landlord who is better informed about their responsibilities, including ensuring safe living
conditions, honoring tenant rights, and handling any disputes fairly and transparently.

Testimony in Opposition of LD 990: "Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an
Optional Online Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations"
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and the distinguished members of the Committee on Committee On Judiciary, my name is Harris Van Pate and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to testify in opposition to LD 990.
While the intention behind this bill may appear benign--providing information to landlords through an optional online registry--LD 990 represents a subtle but concerning step toward expanding the administrative state and normalizing government involvement in private residential arrangements.
This bill directs the Office of the Attorney General to develop and promote an online registry for landlords who rent rooms in their own homes--not corporate landlords or large property managers, but ordinary Mainers seeking to make ends meet by renting out a room. These individuals should not be treated like commercial housing providers, nor should they be encouraged to register voluntarily with the state.
Even if this registry is framed as "optional," it sends a message that private property owners are expected to enter their names into a government database to receive basic information about their rights. Over time, what begins as a voluntary initiative often becomes the foundation for future mandates. This is particularly concerning in the current political climate, where additional landlord regulations are frequently proposed at local and state levels, further burdening housing production and discouraging people from developing housing.1
Suppose the state believes educational materials for resident landlords are valuable. In that case, it can make that information publicly available--without creating a government-run registry that could later be weaponized for enforcement or regulation. The additional bureaucratic effort required to develop and maintain such a platform is unnecessary and wasteful, mainly when private legal resources, nonprofits, or existing housing organizations can publish these materials.
Ultimately, LD 990 promotes a paternalistic approach to governance. Maine should work to reduce red tape, lower housing costs, and empower property owners, not encourage them to submit their personal information to a government registry under the guise of education.
1 https://mainepolicy.org/research/under-construction/executive-summary/

For these reasons, we respectfully urge the committee to vote "Ought Not to Pass" on LD 990. Thank you for your time and consideration.
10038881:
LD 990 -- Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an Optional Online Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations
Testimony of John Brautigam, Esq. for Legal Services for Maine Elders Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary
March 24, 2025
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary.
My name is John Brautigam, and I am here today on behalf of Legal Services for Maine Elders. LSE provides free legal help for Mainers aged 60 and older when their basic human needs are at stake.
It was my intention to provide verbal testimony today but I was testifying in a different committee when this bill came up in the Judiciary Committee. I have just a brief comment, as follows.
In our experience, it is not uncommon for a person to rent out a room or other small portion of their home to earn some extra income. The nature of our work is that we see older people renting in this way, but undoubtedly it is more widespread.
We also see many such "landlords" who are not fully aware of the legal ramifications of these arrangements. They may not appreciate that many of the legal obligations binding on the landlord of a 100-unit high rise apartment building may also apply to these more limited arrangements.
Both the renters and the landlords in these circumstances would often benefit from clear, concise and reliable information about their respective rights and responsibilities. The Attorney General's Office and a few other entities provide resources regarding the legal obligations in landlord-tenant relationships, but we are not aware of any public education effort specifically focused on this type of arrangement, which may be much more casual. To the extent that this is the goal of LD 990, we think it is worthwhile.
We look forward to reviewing information from the public hearing so that we may better understand the separate concept of an on-line registry.
Thank you.

March 24, 2025
Testimony in support of LD 990, "Resolve, Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to Develop and Promote an Optional Online Registry Informing Landlords of Their Rights and Obligations"
Good afternoon Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary. I am here to testify in support of LD 990.
My name is Paul Armstrong and I live in the town of Palermo in Waldo County. I am the constituent who brought this issue to Senator Curry's attention after I went through the nightmare of trying to evict someone whom I had rented a room to in my own home.
I lobbied here for the Home Share bill in Maine, this bill will help many seniors, and those in need of affordable housing, get together. It is aimed at helping seniors rent out a room in their homes at a discounted rate in exchange for help around the home along with companionship to fight isolation. I'd like to point out that even renting a single room in your own domicile makes you a full fledged landlord according to the law- on par with someone renting a complex full of apartments.
My going through the eviction process was a long and costly ordeal, not to mention the mental and emotional strain of having to share my home with someone who was disrespectful, spiteful, obviously unwanted and fundamentally living there for free during the eviction process. I could not afford to hire a lawyer and proceeded on my own. I tried my best to do the due diligence of learning the proper and legal procedures for executing an eviction. The majority of information I found through contacting professionals, legal services, and searching the internet was geared for the person(s) being evicted not the person(s) looking to evict. I also learned that most of the people facing evictions may receive free legal help and even representation but absolutely nothing of the like available for landlords.
I believe that the Office of the Attorney General in Maine should most definitely create a site that is geared towards the Mainer who wants to rent a room in their own home which will explain all the rights and obligations as landlords in simple straight forward language. It should point out the pitfalls they may face and the technicalities many lose on or the process delayed with- such as, I was informed by the court I `filed" the papers 4 hours before I was supposed to and had to start the entire procedure over including having to pay all the fees again!
Personally, I don't feel having a registry is the best idea with this proposal. Yes, I understand that it could open the communication door if the laws change, however in this day and age of seniors not comfortable with the internet and the horror stories of sites being hacked and information stolen, I oppose this portion of the bill.
By voting ought to pass on LD 990, Maine has the opportunity to increase the knowledge landlords in Maine have for the better. My thanks to Senator Curry for his leadership on this important issue and I thank this committee for its time and consideration.

Paul Armstrong
